description:
**The claims that justify this project's existence are all environmental, and none has been tested in the environment it concerns.** Everything up to `80` runs in a test harness. This tasklist runs it where it actually has to work.

What is genuinely being tested, from `docs/reference/platform-constraints.md`:

- **App suspension** — JS does not run while suspended, which is the entire reason the RN surface is a control plane only. Prove a transfer continues while the app is backgrounded.
- **Process death and relaunch** — the durable registry plus launch reconciler exist for exactly this. *"Close the app, reopen it, find the upload still there and still cancelable."*
- **Storage reclamation mid-transfer** — the original bug. iOS reclaiming the purgeable `Caches` directory is why staging goes to Application Support.
- **Android's 6h/24h `dataSync` budget** — a multi-hour upload must survive budget exhaustion by design, not by luck.
- **iOS 17+ native transport vs the pre-17 fallback** — two transports, and only one of them is exercised on a modern simulator by default.
- **Network transitions** — wifi to cellular, and loss mid-flight.

**Simulators and emulators do not test most of this.** Background execution budgets, real storage pressure and radio transitions need physical devices. Where a case can only be checked on a device, say so and record the result rather than substituting a simulator run that proves something weaker.

userStories.title: A written environment matrix, with each cell's verdict and how it was reached
userStories.description: The deliverable is the evidence, not a green tick. State which cells needed a physical device.
acceptanceCriteria: A matrix document covers OS versions × transport × source type × interruption mode, and is linked from `docs/README.md`.
Every cell records how it was verified: automated, manual-on-device, or NOT YET VERIFIED.
Cells that a simulator or emulator cannot honestly cover are marked as such rather than filled with a weaker substitute.
The iOS 17+ native transport and the pre-17 TUSKit fallback are BOTH exercised.
userStories.notes: Added docs/reference/environment-matrix.md and linked it from docs/README.md; 10 OS/transport/source rows × 4 interruption cells explicitly record NOT YET VERIFIED physical-device gaps. Swift build green; Amphora path tests 44 passed; TypeScript typecheck passed; Gradle skipped because no Gradle toolchain was available.

userStories.title: The four environmental claims are each demonstrated
userStories.description: Backgrounding, process death, storage reclamation, and the Android dataSync budget.
acceptanceCriteria: A transfer continues while the app is backgrounded, on both platforms, evidenced by a captured log or recording.
An upload survives process death and is resumable AND cancelable after relaunch — the README's stated promise, tested literally.
Storage reclaimed mid-transfer produces a clean typed failure and no corrupted upload — the original bug, proven retired.
An Android upload spanning the 6h `dataSync` budget continues correctly across budget exhaustion.
A wifi-to-cellular transition mid-transfer does not corrupt or restart the upload.
userStories.notes: Added docs/reference/environment-evidence.md and linked it from docs/README.md. Swift build + AmphoraPathTests: green, 44 passed; TypeScript typecheck: green. The evidence ledger records automated protocol/state and typed storage observations plus explicit NOT YET VERIFIED physical-device gaps for background suspension, Android 6h dataSync exhaustion, and Wi-Fi→cellular handoff; Gradle was skipped because no Gradle toolchain was available.
